statement: The universe loader shall read a TOML document whose only permitted top-level keys are `defaults` (a table) and `asset` (an array of tables); when no path is given it shall read the packaged `universe.toml` (shipped verbatim in contracts/universe.toml) and label it `packaged universe.toml` in messages, otherwise it shall label it with the path exactly as given.

The `[defaults]` table shall accept only the keys `store` (default `data`) and `currency` (default `USD`); each, when present, shall be a non-empty string, and an absent `[defaults]` table shall resolve to those two defaults.

Each `[[asset]]` table shall accept only the keys `name`, `asset_class`, `currency`, `threshold`, `enabled` and `source`; `name` and `asset_class` are required non-empty strings, `currency` defaults to the `[defaults]` currency, `enabled` defaults to true, and `source` is a non-empty array of tables.

The universe shall accept exactly three `asset_class` values and map each to the store `asset_type`: `stock` -> `stock`, `crypto` -> `crypto`, `bond_etf` -> `etf`; the store asset_type vocabulary is the sorted set of mapped values `['crypto', 'etf', 'stock']`.

When an asset carries `threshold`, the loader shall accept any integer or float (not a boolean) and carry it as a float; when absent it shall default to -0.05; the value is documentation only and shall drive no behaviour of any command.
rationale: the per-class threshold stays a conscious later knob; it is carried as documentation and never read by the loader

statement: Each `[[asset.source]]` table shall accept only the keys `provider`, `symbol`, `path`, `exchange`, `start`, `end`, `kind`, `enabled`, `modeled` and `note`; `provider` (one of `eodhd`, `binance`, `yahoo-csv`) and `symbol` are required non-empty strings, `kind` defaults to `eod`, `enabled` to true, `modeled` to false, `note` is an optional non-empty string, and the source inherits the asset's currency.

When a source declares no `exchange`, the loader shall set the store partition tag from the provider: `eodhd` -> `eodhd`, `binance` -> `binance`, `yahoo-csv` -> `yahoo`; a declared `exchange` shall be a non-empty string and is used verbatim as the store partition tag.
rationale: the venue tag, not a listing exchange - the EODHD listing exchange lives in the symbol suffix

statement: When a collector source (eodhd, binance) declares `start` or `end`, the loader shall normalise a TOML local date, or a string accepted by Python 3.11+ `date.fromisoformat` (e.g. `2024-01-02` or `20240102`), to `YYYY-MM-DD`; a TOML date-time shall be carried as its full ISO text (e.g. `2024-01-01T10:00:00+00:00`); an absent key shall be carried as null.

When a source's provider is `yahoo-csv`, the loader shall require `path` (non-empty string, resolved relative to the working directory at run time) and shall carry no `start`/`end` keys; when the provider is `eodhd` or `binance` the loader shall carry `start` and `end` (possibly null) and no `path`.

The loader shall enforce the modeled-source marker per asset: a `modeled = true` source must be enabled; at most one enabled source may be modeled; an enabled asset with two or more enabled sources must mark exactly one modeled; an enabled asset must have at least one enabled source; a disabled asset is exempt from the two last rules.
rationale: the series that feeds the binning must be deterministic per enabled asset

statement: The loader shall return one normalised document `{"defaults": {"store", "currency"}, "assets": [...]}` where each asset carries `name`, `asset_class`, `asset_type`, `currency`, `threshold` (float), `enabled` and `sources`, and each source carries `provider`, `kind`, `enabled`, `modeled`, `exchange`, `symbol`, `currency`, then `note` only when declared, then either `path` (yahoo-csv) or `start` and `end` (collector sources), in universe file order.

The loader shall stop at the first violation, checking in this order: TOML syntax; top-level keys; `[defaults]` is a table; `[defaults]` keys; `store`; `currency`; `asset` is a non-empty array; then per asset in file order: is a table, keys, `name`, `asset_class` presence then value, `threshold`, `currency`, `source` non-empty array, `enabled`, then per source in order: is a table, keys, `provider` presence then value, `kind`, `symbol`, eodhd dot rule, `modeled`, `enabled`, `exchange`, `note`, `path`, `start`, `end`, CSV/collector key rules, start-after-end; then the asset's modeled rules; after all assets: duplicate names, then duplicate store coordinates.
If the universe text is not valid TOML, then the loader shall raise UniverseError `{origin}: not valid TOML: {parser message}` where the parser message is Python `tomllib`'s exception text.

If a table carries a key outside its permitted set, then the loader shall raise UniverseError `{where}: unknown key(s) {sorted unknown list}; allowed: {sorted allowed list}`, with `where` = `{origin}` (top level), `{origin} [defaults]`, `asset #{n}` (1-based, asset keys are checked before its name is known) or `asset '{name}' source #{n}`; lists render as Python lists of quoted strings.

If the document's shape is wrong, then the loader shall raise UniverseError with exactly one of: `{origin}: [defaults] must be a table`; `{origin}: no [[asset]] entries` (absent, empty or non-array `asset`); `asset #{n}: must be a table`; `asset '{name}': needs at least one [[asset.source]]` (absent, empty or non-array `source`); `asset '{name}' source #{n}: must be a table`.

If a scalar is wrong, then the loader shall raise UniverseError with exactly one of: `{where}: missing required key '{key}'`; `{where}: {key} must be a non-empty string, got {value!r}` (where is `[defaults]` for the defaults table); `{where}: {key} must be a boolean, got {value!r}` (enabled); `{where}: modeled must be a boolean, got {value!r}`; `{where}: threshold must be a number (documentation only), got {value!r}`; `{where}: {key} must be an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), got {value!r}`.

If an enumerated value is unknown, then the loader shall raise UniverseError with exactly one of: `asset '{name}': unknown asset_class {value!r}; allowed: ['bond_etf', 'crypto', 'stock']`; `{where}: unknown provider {value!r}; allowed: ['eodhd', 'binance', 'yahoo-csv']`; `{where}: kind {value!r} is not supported - only ['eod']; a non-EOD load is a new data contract, not a config value`.

If an `eodhd` source's symbol contains no `.`, then the loader shall raise UniverseError `{where}: eodhd symbols must be canonical TICKER.EXCHANGE (e.g. AAPL.US, BTC-USD.CC), got {symbol!r} - bare tickers would blur store coordinates and the crypto/raw basis split`.
rationale: bare tickers would blur store coordinates and the crypto/raw basis split

statement: If window keys are misplaced or inverted, then the loader shall raise UniverseError with exactly one of: `{where}: start/end apply to collector sources only; a CSV import is whole-file`; `{where}: path applies to yahoo-csv sources only`; `{where}: start {start} is after end {end}` (compared as normalised ISO strings).

If the modeled-source rules of the universe are violated, then the loader shall raise UniverseError with exactly one of: `asset '{name}': a modeled source must be enabled`; `asset '{name}': exactly one enabled source may be modeled = true, got {k}`; `asset '{name}': {k} enabled sources but none marked modeled = true - the binning's feeder must be deterministic (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md SS7.7)`; `asset '{name}': enabled but has no enabled source - nothing would feed the binning; to pause the asset, set enabled = false on the asset itself`.

If two assets share a name, then the loader shall raise UniverseError `{origin}: duplicate asset name(s) {sorted names}`; if two assets declare the same (exchange tag, symbol) store coordinate, then it shall raise `{origin}: store series {exchange}/{symbol} is claimed by both {first owner!r} and {second owner!r} - two assets may never write the same partition` (one asset may repeat a coordinate across its own sources).
rationale: two assets may never write the same partition

statement: If an explicit universe path does not exist, then the command shall terminate with an unhandled FileNotFoundError traceback on stderr and exit code 1 (the error is not wrapped in the `{command}: ` prefix).

Every collector shall perform HTTP through a transport offering `request(method, url, params) -> (status, text)` and `close()`; the live transport shall use a requests session with a 30 s timeout and convert connection errors and timeouts into a retryable TransportConnectionError whose text has the token redacted; each collector shall rate-limit live traffic to 1000 requests per sliding 60 s window (sleeping until the oldest request leaves the window) and 100000 per UTC day, beyond which it raises DailyBudgetExhausted `daily API budget of 100000 spent ({UTC date}); the per-minute window cannot lend quota across days`.
rationale: the daily quota is enforced as a daily budget, not fed in as a per-minute rate

statement: The recorded-fixture identity of a request shall be `{"method": METHOD upper-cased, "path": the URL's path component, "params": {name: str(value)}}` over the request parameters minus `api_token`, sorted by name.

The fixture recorder shall write one file per request named `{slug}_{digest}.json` where slug is the key's path with leading/trailing `/` stripped and inner `/` replaced by `_`, and digest is the first 10 hex characters of SHA-256 over `json.dumps(key, sort_keys=True)` (Python default separators, ASCII-escaped) encoded UTF-8; the file content shall be `json.dumps({"request": key, "response": {"status": int, "json": body}}, indent=1, sort_keys=True)` plus a newline, and recording shall refuse with CollectorError `refusing to write fixture: secret material in {path} response/request` when a registered secret occurs in that text.

The fixture replayer shall load every `*.json` file under its directory recursively except files named `manifest.json`, key each by its `request` object, answer a matching request with the recorded `status` and the recorded `json` re-serialised as text, and raise CollectorError `no recorded fixture for {METHOD} {path} {params dict}` followed by a newline, `known fixtures:` and one line per known key (`  {path} {params dict}`, sorted) for any other request.

When a collector request answers HTTP 429 or any status >= 500, or the transport raises a connection error, the collector shall retry up to 4 times (5 attempts in all), sleeping `2.0 * 2**attempt` seconds after attempt 0, 1, 2, 3, and shall acquire the rate limiter before every attempt.
rationale: retries and rate limiting live in the collector, not the transport, so they are exercised identically for live and replayed traffic

statement: If a collector request cannot succeed, then it shall raise CollectorError with exactly one of: `{label}: HTTP {status} after {attempts} attempts` (retryable status exhausted; attempts = the attempt count of JDL-027); `{label}: network failure after {attempts} attempts: {redacted error}`; `{label}: HTTP {status}: {first 200 characters of the body, token redacted as ***}` (any other non-200); `{label}: response is not JSON: {first 200 characters, redacted}`; the label is `eod {SYM}`, `splits {SYM}`, `div {SYM}` or `klines {symbol}`.

The EODHD collector shall call `GET {base}/eod/{SYM}` with params `api_token`, `fmt=json`, `period=d`, `order=a`, plus `from={start}` and `to={end}` only when given; `GET {base}/splits/{SYM}` and `GET {base}/div/{SYM}` with `api_token` and `fmt=json` only; base defaults to `https://eodhd.com/api` with any trailing `/` removed, so recorded fixture paths are `/api/eod/{SYM}`, `/api/splits/{SYM}`, `/api/div/{SYM}`.

If the EODHD collector is constructed with no API key argument and an empty or unset EODHD_API_KEY, then construction shall raise ValueError `EODHD API key required: pass api_key= or set EODHD_API_KEY` before any session is opened.
rationale: config errors must fail first, and without opening a session

statement: The EODHD symbol normaliser shall pass a symbol containing `.` through unchanged; map `BASE/QUOTE` to `{BASE}{QUOTE}.FOREX` (upper-cased) when both sides are in the fiat set (USD EUR GBP JPY CHF AUD NZD CAD SEK NOK DKK PLN CZK HUF TRY ZAR MXN SGD HKD CNY INR BRL KRW RUB), else to `{BASE}-{QUOTE}.CC` when QUOTE is in the crypto-quote set (USD USDT EUR BTC ETH BUSD USDC), else raise CollectorError `cannot infer exchange for pair symbol {symbol!r}`; any other bare ticker gains `.US`.

When the EODHD `/eod/` response is not a JSON list, the collector shall raise CollectorError `eod {SYM}: expected a JSON list`; otherwise it shall drop every row whose `close` is absent, null, zero or negative, keep the first row per `date` string, and return the surviving provider rows unmodified, sorted ascending by `date` string.
rationale: close<=0 rows are provider glitch rows

statement: The EODHD collector shall turn each `/splits/` entry `{date, split}` into a split event with date = `date`, ratio = new/old parsed from `split` as `NEW/OLD` floats (e.g. `4/1` -> 4.0, `3.000000/2.000000` -> 1.5), and the split string kept verbatim, returned sorted ascending by date (stable); an unparseable string shall raise ValueError `unparseable split string: {s!r}` and a zero side `degenerate split string: {s!r}`.
The EODHD collector shall return the `/div/` entries verbatim (every provider field kept), sorted ascending by their `date` string (a missing date sorts as the empty string).

The EODHD collector shall declare its volume basis `split_adjusted` (served volume is already forward split-adjusted while prices are raw) and the Binance collector shall declare `raw`; the declaration is consulted only when a series is stored with price_basis `raw`.
rationale: measured at a live re-record: /eod/ prices arrive raw but volume arrives already split-adjusted

statement: The Binance collector shall call `GET https://api.binance.com/api/v3/klines` with params `symbol` (the universe symbol verbatim), `interval=1d`, `limit=1000`, `startTime` (only when a cursor exists) and `endTime` (only when an end is given), needs no key, and exposes its page limit (1000) as the collector attribute `limit`.

The Binance collector shall convert a start date to `startTime` = Unix milliseconds of that date at 00:00 UTC and an end date to `endTime` = Unix milliseconds of that date at 00:00 UTC + 86 400 000 - 1.

The Binance collector shall page ascending: the first page uses startTime = start (omitted without a start); a page ends the loop when it is empty, holds fewer rows than `limit`, or its last openTime + one day in milliseconds (the day length of JDL-037) exceeds endTime; otherwise the next page's startTime is the last openTime + one day; more than 100 pages shall raise CollectorError `pagination exceeded 100 pages - refusing to truncate silently; raise max_pages if the range is real`; a non-list page shall raise CollectorError `klines {symbol}: expected a JSON list`.

The Binance collector shall map each kline array to the bar `{date: UTC date of element 0 (ms) as YYYY-MM-DD, open: float(e1), high: float(e2), low: float(e3), close: float(e4), adjusted_close: float(e4), volume: float(e5)}`, drop bars with close <= 0, keep the first bar per date, and return them sorted ascending by date; volume is in base-asset units.

The corporate-actions store shall keep one JSON file per symbol and kind at `{store}/corporate_actions/splits/{SYMBOL}.json` and `{store}/corporate_actions/dividends/{SYMBOL}.json` (every `/` in the symbol replaced by `_`), each written with 2-space indentation plus a trailing newline and holding, in this key order, `symbol`, `exchange`, `last_updated` and `splits` or `dividends`.

Each stored split item shall be `{"date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "split": the provider split string, "ratio": float}` (split string `{ratio:g}/1` when an event carries none), sorted ascending by date; reading splits back shall take `date` and `ratio` from the file (the stored ratio drives every calculation, the split string is never re-parsed).

When corporate actions are synced for a symbol, the program shall fetch splits, then dividends, then write the splits file, then the dividends file, each with exchange `eodhd` and the same kind of stamp, and report the two counts; the writes are plain truncating writes (not atomic).

The `last_updated` stamp shall be the real wall-clock UTC time at the moment the file is written, formatted as naive ISO 8601 plus `Z` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ`, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` when microseconds are zero); an injected run clock never reaches the stamp.

When a symbol's actions file is absent, reading it shall yield no events (an empty list) and no stamp (null); a stamp shall be read by replacing `Z` with `+00:00` and parsing ISO 8601, and its UTC calendar date is what every freshness rule compares.
rationale: absent = no known actions, so symbols without splits don't force API calls

statement: The cumulative split factor of a row shall be computed in float64 starting from 1.0 and multiplying, for each split event in stored (ascending-date) order, by that event's ratio when the row's UTC calendar date is strictly before the event's date.

A row dated on a split's effective date shall not include that split in its factor (it already trades at the new basis), so the first row of a series older than every split carries the product of all ratios.
rationale: the effective date is the first session at the new price basis

statement: When a series is adjusted, each of open, high, low and close shall be set to its `*_raw` value divided by the row's factor (float64 division), and `cumulative_split_factor` shall be set to the factor.

When a series is adjusted, volume shall be set to `volume_raw` multiplied by the row's factor (float64), so a volume whose raw-ization is not exactly invertible stays non-integral (e.g. 100000 / 10.5 * 10.5 = 99999.99999999999).

The adjustment shall read only the `*_raw` columns and the split events, carry every other column unchanged, and return a new frame, so adjusting an already adjusted series with the same events is a fixed point and re-adjusting after the event list changes re-derives every main column from raw.
rationale: the NJAPMP pass divided the stored main columns in place on every run, compounding corruption; a pure function of raw + events makes that unrepresentable and doubles as the repair path

statement: Dividends shall never enter any price, volume or factor calculation (split-only policy); they are stored and never applied.

If the adjustment is asked to process a frame whose `price_basis` column holds any value other than `raw`, then it shall raise AdjustmentRefused `price_basis {sorted non-raw values} is already adjusted at the provider - applying split events would double-adjust (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §2)`.
rationale: applying split events to pre-adjusted prices would double-adjust

statement: If a split event's ratio is non-finite or <= 0, then the adjustment shall raise AdjustmentRefused `split {date} has degenerate ratio {ratio!r}`; if any `*_raw` column or `datetime` is missing it shall raise AdjustmentRefused `cannot adjust without immutable raw columns: missing {list}`.

The price basis of a stored series shall be resolved from the provider and the DECLARED asset_type only, never from the symbol suffix: eodhd + asset_type crypto -> `split_adjusted`; eodhd + stock or etf -> `raw`; binance -> `split_adjusted`; yahoo-csv import -> `split_adjusted`; a `split_adjusted` series never receives split events.
rationale: a declared crypto outside the .CC namespace stored raw would be put through the split pass - the double-adjustment class

statement: When bars are stored with price_basis `raw` from a collector whose volume basis is `split_adjusted`, the program shall set `volume_raw` = served volume / factor computed from the splits known at ingest (float64 division) and then derive volume = volume_raw * factor per the adjustment; with volume basis `raw`, `volume_raw` = served volume; any other volume basis value shall raise StoreError `unknown volume_basis {value!r}`.
rationale: true raw is split-invariant, so a split synced later repairs through re-adjustment exactly like prices; the flip side is that splits must be synced before the first load of a split-history symbol

statement: When bars are stored with price_basis `split_adjusted`, each main column (open, high, low, close, volume) and its `*_raw` twin shall both hold the served value and `cumulative_split_factor` shall be 1.0.

When a bar is stored, `adjusted_close` shall be the bar's `adjusted_close` value whenever the bar carries that key (a NaN value stays NaN), else its `close` (for Yahoo CSVs the `Adj Close` column, always carried), and `adjustment_factor` shall be adjusted_close / close_raw (float64).

The market-data store shall keep each series under `{store}/market_data/exchange={exchange tag}/symbol={symbol}/` with one Parquet file per calendar year of the UTC session date at `year={YYYY}/data.parquet` (snappy compression), and a lock file `.lock` in the symbol directory created on the first write.

When a year file is written, the store shall write `data.parquet.tmp` beside it and atomically rename it over `data.parquet`, remove any leftover `*.tmp` year files of that series before writing, and, when pruning, delete stale year files only after every new file is in place; every read-modify-write of a series shall hold an exclusive advisory lock on its `.lock` file, waiting up to 300 s polling every 0.5 s and then raising StoreError `{exchange}/{symbol}: another writer holds the store lock after 300s ({lock path})`.
rationale: a reader never sees a torn file and no instant exists where raw history is only in memory; a stuck lock holder must be surfaced, never silently queued behind

statement: Every stored row shall carry exactly these 21 columns in this order and Parquet type: timestamp int64; datetime timestamp[ms, tz=UTC]; open, high, low, close, volume float64; symbol, exchange, asset_type, asset_subtype string; adjustment_factor, open_raw, high_raw, low_raw, close_raw, volume_raw, adjusted_close, cumulative_split_factor float64; currency, price_basis string.

When bars are stored, each bar's `date` string shall be parsed as a UTC instant (format inferred from the first bar; a date-only string gives that day's 00:00 UTC, a time of day if present is kept, never truncated); `datetime` shall hold it at millisecond resolution, and `timestamp` shall hold the Unix epoch in whole SECONDS (e.g. 2024-01-02 -> 1704153600) - the value the pinned environment produces for date-only strings, despite the column being documented as milliseconds.

If any bar date cannot be parsed in the format of the first bar, then storing shall raise StoreError `unparseable dates cannot be stored: {list of at most the first 5 offending values}` and write nothing.

When bars are stored, `symbol` shall be the store symbol, `exchange` the store partition tag (not the provider name), `asset_type` the declared store asset_type, `asset_subtype` the empty string, `currency` the leg's currency, and `price_basis` the resolved basis, identical on every row of the write.

When a series is read, the store shall concatenate its year files in path order, sort rows by timestamp (stable), keep the first row of any duplicated timestamp, and number rows 0..n-1; a series with no year file shall read as a zero-row frame with the 21 columns.

The latest stored session of a series shall be the maximum UTC date in the lexicographically last `year=` file, or none when the series has no file; the newest-n stored sessions shall be the n most recent distinct UTC dates (all of them when fewer exist), ascending.

When served bars are reconciled into a series, the store shall compare each served row whose timestamp is already stored on the six as-served columns open_raw, high_raw, low_raw, close_raw, volume_raw, adjusted_close (exact equality, two NaNs equal), replace the stored row wholesale when any differs, keep the stored row untouched when none differs, append served rows with new timestamps, and never touch stored rows the served set does not contain; derived columns are not compared.
rationale: derived columns re-derive from the as-served ones and are excluded on purpose; raw-ization makes a re-served pre-split bar comparable, so an unchanged serve produces zero phantom revisions

statement: The reconcile shall consider every timestamp it is handed, including served rows older than the requested window: frozen-first-seen history outside the tail is enforced only by the fetch window, never by the store.
rationale: this method only ever considers the timestamps it is handed

statement: Each revised cell shall be reported as `{"date": served row's UTC date YYYY-MM-DD, "column": as-served column name, "stored": float, "served": float}`, ordered by served row order and, within a row, in the column order open_raw, high_raw, low_raw, close_raw, volume_raw, adjusted_close; `served` is the value as it would be stored (after volume raw-ization).

The reconcile shall report as its bar count the number of served bars handed to it (re-served unchanged rows included), shall write nothing when no row is replaced and none is new, shall write only the year files of replaced or new rows otherwise, and shall write every served row (no revisions) when the series is empty.

When a raw-basis series is re-adjusted, the store shall, under the series lock, read the whole series, re-derive it through the adjustment with the given split events, rewrite every year file (pruning stale ones) only when any value changed, and report the row count; an empty series shall raise StoreError `nothing stored for {exchange}/{symbol}`.
rationale: the daily no-new-bars case costs a read and a compare, never a rewrite

statement: When a Yahoo CSV is imported, the store shall require the columns Date, Open, High, Low, Close, Adj Close, Volume (else StoreError `{csv path}: not a 7-column Yahoo CSV, missing {list}`), map each CSV row to a bar (Adj Close -> adjusted_close), store every row - zero-volume and NaN rows included - with price_basis `split_adjusted` and volume basis `raw`, REPLACE the whole stored series (prune stale years), and report the number of CSV rows (duplicate dates are counted but only the first is stored).
rationale: the load policy belongs to the seam, not the store

statement: The exported frame shall have exactly the columns Date, Open, High, Low, Close, Adj Close, Volume, one row per stored row in stored order, with Date = the UTC date of `datetime` as `YYYY-MM-DD` text, Open/High/Low/Close = the adjusted main columns, Adj Close = `adjusted_close`, all float64.

The exported Volume column shall be int64 when the series is non-empty and every volume is finite and integral, and float64 (values unchanged) otherwise - a single non-integral or NaN volume makes the whole column float64.
rationale: mirrors pd.read_csv's inference so the seam is bit-exact against a CSV load of the same data

statement: The export shall pass every stored row through, zero-volume and NaN rows included, and shall apply no load policy of its own.
rationale: the seam owns the zero-volume/NaN drop policy

statement: The downstream seam that consumes the exported frame (outside this program) applies the load policy the validation notes announce: it sorts by date, drops rows whose Date does not parse, drops zero-volume rows and drops rows with a NaN in any column; this program implements that policy nowhere except where status emulates the zero-volume and NaN drop (JDL-122, JDL-120).
When `export` writes its CSV, it shall write the frame with a header line and no index column, floats in shortest round-trip form (e.g. `19.84952380952381`, `100000.0`), int64 volumes as integers.

When a frame is validated, a missing required column (Date, Open, High, Low, Close, Adj Close, Volume) shall produce the single error `missing required columns: {list}` and stop; extra columns shall produce the note `extra columns {list} are carried through; NaNs in them will drop rows at load (the transform drops any-NaN rows)`.

When a frame is validated, a price column (Open, High, Low, Close, Adj Close) or Volume shall be non-numeric when numeric coercion yields more missing values than the column already had, producing one error `non-numeric values in {list}` for all such columns; the negative, High<Low, zero-volume, NaN-row and clean-row checks run only when no column is non-numeric.

When a frame is validated, Date values that do not parse shall produce the error `no parseable dates in 'Date'` (and stop) when none parses, else the note `{n} unparseable date(s) - those rows drop at load`; duplicated parsed dates shall produce the error `{n} duplicate date(s) - forbidden by the contract`; non-ascending parsed dates shall produce the note `dates not sorted ascending - the load transform sorts`.

When a frame is validated with all columns numeric, it shall add the errors `negative prices in {columns}`, `negative values in Volume` and `{n} row(s) with High < Low`, and the notes `{n} zero-volume row(s) - dropped at load by policy`, `{n} row(s) with NaN - dropped at load` (NaN in any required column) and `{clean} clean row(s) < recommended minimum {min} (720 warm-up + 395 lags) - the default counter window needs more history (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §1)`, where clean counts rows with a parsed date, non-zero volume and no NaN among the six numeric columns.
The recommended minimum clean-row count shall be 1115 (720 warm-up rows + 30 offset + 365 period), overridable by `validate --min-rows`; the clean-row note appears only when clean < minimum.
rationale: 720 warm-up rows before the first counter + offset 30 + period 365 forward lags consumed by the feature block

statement: The validation report shall render as one line `ERROR: {error}` per error, then one line `note:  {note}` (two spaces) per note, each list in the order the checks run, or the single line `contract: clean`; the report is ok exactly when it holds no error.

The differential shall align the two frames on identical Date strings (each sorted by Date) and, for Open, High, Low, Close, Adj Close and Volume over the common dates, compute rel = |a - b| / max(|a|, |b|) with a zero denominator replaced by 1.0, rel = 0 when both values are NaN and rel = infinity when exactly one is; a cell is beyond tolerance when rel > tolerance (default 1e-4).

The differential report shall be the lines `differential: {A} vs {B} (relative tolerance {tol:g})`, `rows: {nA} in {A}, {nB} in {B}, {nC} dates in common`, for each side with unmatched dates `only in {label}: {n} date(s): {first 5 sorted, comma-separated}` plus ` (+{n-5} more)` when n > 5, then per column either `{col}: within tolerance (max {max rel:.3%})` or `{col}: {k}/{nC} beyond tolerance, worst {rel:.3%} on {date} ({A}={a!r}, {B}={b!r})` (numpy scalar repr, e.g. `np.float64(10.5)`, worst = first maximum), then `VERDICT: within tolerance, aligned` or `VERDICT: {cells} cell(s) beyond tolerance, {unmatched} unmatched date(s) - review before scale-out`.

The sync and status commands shall select legs as every enabled asset (universe order) x every enabled source of it (source order), keeping only assets named by the asset filter and sources whose provider is in the provider filter when those filters are given; each leg carries the keys and derivations of contracts/leg.md.

If an asset filter names an asset absent from the universe (disabled assets count as present), then selection shall raise SyncError `unknown asset {name!r}; universe has {sorted names}`; if a provider filter is not one of eodhd, binance, yahoo-csv, it shall raise `unknown provider {name!r}; allowed: ['eodhd', 'binance', 'yahoo-csv']`; if no leg survives, it shall raise `selection matched no enabled asset/source legs`; asset filters are checked (in the given order) before provider filters.
rationale: a filter that matches nothing is a typo, not an empty day's work

statement: A leg shall be actions-eligible exactly when its provider is `eodhd` and its DECLARED asset_type is not `crypto`, whatever the symbol suffix (a `.CC` symbol declared stock is eligible; an EODHD symbol outside `.CC` declared crypto is not).
rationale: eligibility reads the declared class, like the end-guard and the basis; a .CC symbol declared non-crypto is a mis-declaration whose fix is the declaration

statement: If the sync tail is smaller than 1, then the sync shall raise SyncError `tail must be >= 1 session, got {tail}` before any selection or store access; the default tail is 10 sessions.

The sync shall take `today` as the UTC calendar date of the run clock (the real current UTC time unless a clock is injected) once at the start of the run, and use it for the crypto end-guard, the actions gate and the today-dated-bar check of every leg.
When no store path is given, the sync and status commands shall use the universe's `defaults.store` (relative to the working directory).

For an actions-eligible leg, the sync shall run, in this order: the actions gate and (when due) the corporate-actions sync; reading the stored splits; the bar fetch; the reconcile; the re-adjustment; so a failure of the bar fetch leaves the refreshed actions files in place, and a failure of the actions sync fetches no bars.
rationale: for raw-basis EODHD series the order (sync-actions BEFORE load) is load-bearing for volume raw-ization

statement: The actions gate shall refresh an actions-eligible leg's corporate actions when force-actions is set, or no splits stamp exists, or the stamp's UTC date is earlier than `today`; otherwise it shall skip the refresh and contribute `actions fresh; ` to the leg detail.
rationale: a calendar date cannot be missed by a second; a run straddling midnight UTC stamps tomorrow and skips one refresh, absorbed by the status side's two-session tolerance

statement: An actions-eligible leg shall reconcile and re-adjust with the split events read from the actions store after the gate; every other leg shall use no split events.

The fetch start of a collector leg shall be the universe `start` (or none) while the series has no stored row, and otherwise the oldest of the newest `tail` stored sessions (the tail-refresh window), as `YYYY-MM-DD`; the universe `start` is never read again once the series has rows.
rationale: start is a first-fill floor only

statement: The fetch end of a collector leg shall be the earlier (ISO string minimum) of the universe `end` and, for a leg whose DECLARED asset_type is crypto (any provider), the end-guard `today - 1 day`; with neither, the fetch is open-ended; the universe `end` caps every fetch, first fill and tail refresh alike.
rationale: the provider serves the in-progress UTC day; the guard keys on the declared class because a union of provider and suffix tests silently lost the guard for a crypto leg matching neither

statement: When a leg's series has stored rows and its fetch start is later than its fetch end, the sync shall send no bar request, treat the fetch as zero bars, keep the leg green, and add `end {end} predates the stored tail (from {start}); nothing fetched - a pinned window with rows past its end, the fix is the declaration; ` to the detail; an empty series with start > end still sends its request.
rationale: a provider's answer to from > to is undefined; never red, the fix is the declaration

statement: When a first fill (no stored row) of a leg with no universe `start` receives exactly as many bars as the collector's `limit` attribute (Binance's page limit of JDL-036; the EODHD collector has none), the sync shall keep the bars and add `first fill hit the provider page limit ({n} bars, no start declared) - the series is a trailing window, not history; ` to the detail.
rationale: a first fill that lands exactly on the page limit is the provider's default slice, not history

statement: After the reconcile of a leg whose basis is `raw`, the sync shall re-adjust the whole stored series with the leg's split events whenever the series has at least one stored row (also when zero bars were fetched); split_adjusted legs are never re-adjusted.
rationale: gated on the basis, not on actions eligibility; re-adjustment refuses a split_adjusted series by design

statement: The detail of a successful collector leg shall be the concatenation of: the actions part (`{s} split(s), {d} dividend(s); ` after a refresh, `actions fresh; ` after a skipped one, nothing for other legs), the inverted-window part, the page-limit part, `{bars} bar(s), {r} revised cell(s)` (bars = number of bars handed to the reconcile), and `; today-dated bar ingested (pre-close fetch?)` when the newest fetched bar is dated `today`.

A yahoo-csv leg shall import its whole CSV file (path as declared, relative to the working directory) as an overwrite of its store series per JDL-070, with the leg's asset_type and currency, contacting no collector, and its detail shall be `{rows} row(s) imported`.

A binance leg shall never sync corporate actions and shall store price_basis `split_adjusted` with volume basis `raw`, whatever its asset's declared class; whether it is end-guarded follows JDL-094 (the declared class).

When any exception escapes a leg, the sync shall record that leg as failed with detail `{exception class name}: {exception message}` and no revisions, and continue with the next leg; a run is ok exactly when no leg failed, and revisions never fail a run.
rationale: a batch that half-succeeds must never look green

statement: The sync shall construct a collector only when a non-dry-run leg first needs that provider, at most once per provider per run (an injected collector is always used instead), shall construct the EODHD collector with the `--base-url` override when given, and shall close every collector it constructed after the last leg; a failed EODHD construction (no key) fails each eodhd leg in turn without affecting other legs.
rationale: a CSV-only or --dry-run invocation demands no key

statement: The sync shall emit one log line per leg, `ok      {asset} {exchange}/{symbol} [{provider}]: {detail}` or `FAILED  {asset} {exchange}/{symbol} [{provider}]: {detail}`; after an ok line, one line `        revised {date} {column}: {stored:g} -> {served:g}` for each of the first 10 revisions and `        ... {k} more revised cell(s)` when k = count - 10 > 0; and finally `{legs} leg(s), {failed} failed -> store {store path!r}`.

When the sync runs as a dry run, it shall construct no collector, contact no provider and write nothing, emit `plan for store {store path!r} ({n} leg(s)):` then one line per leg of two spaces plus the plan description of JDL-105, and return every leg as ok with detail `planned` and the run ok.
rationale: plans from local store state, so it needs neither network nor key

statement: The plan description of a leg shall be `{asset:>6} {exchange}/{symbol}: import {path} (whole file, idempotent)` for yahoo-csv, else `{asset:>6} {exchange}/{symbol}: {action} ({window})` with action `sync-actions + load` (actions-eligible) or `load`, window `reconcile tail of {tail} session(s) from {start}` (stored rows), `first fill from {start}` (start declared) or `first fill, full history`, then ` to {end}` when an end applies and ` - INVERTED: end predates the stored tail, nothing to fetch` when stored rows exist and start > end.

The sync summary document shall be `{schema_version: 1, legs_total, legs_failed, revised_cells_total, ok, legs: [...]}` with one leg object per leg result in run order holding `asset`, `provider`, `exchange`, `symbol`, `ok`, `detail`, `revised_cells` (count) and `revisions` (each `{date, column, stored, served}` with plain floats); contract sync_summary.schema.json.
rationale: computes nothing new - the loud per-leg prints and this document are two renderings of one set of facts

statement: The status command shall check, in leg order, every selected leg whose provider is not `yahoo-csv` (committed CSV snapshots are not a live feed), and then, for every asset with two or more such legs (in first-appearance order), every leg pair (i, j) with i < j in leg order.
rationale: committed CSV snapshots are not a live feed - nothing to check

statement: The status checks shall take `today` as the UTC calendar date of the real current time (the harness may inject a clock), and shall read the store and the actions store only - no key, no network, no writes.

A source report shall hold, in this key order: `asset`, `exchange`, `symbol`, `alerts`, `warnings`, `notes` (lists of strings), then `declared_class_check` (eodhd legs only), then - for a filled series - `last_session` (YYYY-MM-DD), `missed_sessions` (int), `rows` (int, every stored row) and `resolution` (only when measured); contract status.schema.json.

The source checks shall append their messages in this order: declared class; never filled (which ends the report); staleness; today-dated; zero volume; post-seam continuity; price resolution; phantom jumps (ascending date); corporate-actions freshness.

For an eodhd leg only, the status command shall compare the leg's declared asset_type with the packaged vendor evidence (contracts/classifications.toml, keyed by exchange tag + symbol) and set `declared_class_check` to the verdict; a `disagree` verdict shall add the WARNING `declared class: {message}` and every other verdict the NOTE `declared class: {message}`; neither ever alerts or changes the exit code.
rationale: an alert here would stop every asset's publish over a metadata disagreement; binance and yahoo-csv have no classification endpoint, so a note would read as absent evidence rather than inapplicable

statement: The declared-class verdict shall be: `no_evidence` with message `no vendor classification recorded - run tools/record_classifications.py` when no row exists; `not_comparable` with `vendor type {vt!r} cannot confirm asset_type {at!r}{seen}: the .CC (crypto) and .FOREX namespaces both serve it, so only the symbol's own namespace separates them and the evidence is not independent` for vendor type `Currency`; `unmapped` with `vendor type {vt!r} has no store asset_type counterpart{seen} - no verdict rather than a guess (mapped: ['Common Stock', 'ETF'])` for any other type outside the map; `agree` with `vendor type {vt!r} agrees with declared asset_type {at!r}{seen}` when the mapped type (Common Stock -> stock, ETF -> etf) equals the declaration; else `disagree` with `declared asset_type {at!r} but the vendor says {vt!r} (-> {mapped!r}){seen} for {exchange}/{symbol} - check the asset_class in universe.toml against docs/EVALUATION_ASSET_CLASSIFICATION.md §5 C2`; `{seen}` is `, recorded {last_verified}` when the row has a last_verified date, else empty.
rationale: UNKNOWN is preferable to an incorrect class; Currency is shared by the .CC and .FOREX namespaces, so it confirms nothing

statement: The vendor-classification evidence shall be the packaged `classifications.toml` (shipped verbatim in contracts/classifications.toml; grammar in contracts/classifications.toml.md): top-level keys only `schema` (must be 1), `provenance` and `instrument` (array of tables with keys exchange, symbol, code, query_exchange, vendor_type (all required non-empty strings), isin, name (optional strings, default empty) and last_verified (optional YYYY-MM-DD)), keyed by (exchange, symbol), a duplicate key being an error; the status command always reads the packaged file.
rationale: evidence, never configuration: committed beside the universe so the cross-check compares two committed files, deterministic and offline

statement: When a checked leg's series has no stored row, the status command shall add the ALERT `never filled - no stored rows (jef-data sync first)` and finish that report with no further field or check.

The expected sessions between two dates shall be the calendar days strictly after the first and strictly before the second, keeping only Monday-Friday for asset_type `stock` or `etf` and every day for any other asset_type (crypto); there is no holiday calendar.
rationale: today's bar may legitimately not exist yet; single-day market holidays stay under the default threshold - the conscious no-calendar decision

statement: When the expected sessions between the last stored session and today number at least the staleness threshold (`--staleness`, default 2), the status command shall add the ALERT `stale: {n} expected session(s) missing since {last} (multi-day holidays can trip this - verify before acting)`; `missed_sessions` reports n regardless.
When the last stored session equals today, the status command shall add the NOTE `today-dated bar stored (pre-close serve? the next tail-refresh heals it)`.

When the stored series holds n > 0 rows with volume exactly 0, the status command shall add the NOTE `{n} zero-volume row(s), dropped at the seam by pinned policy`, extended by ` - largest contiguous run {length}, {first}..{last}` when the longest run of consecutive zero-volume rows is longer than 1 row.
rationale: a run is a splice the model receives and a flat total cannot express it; scattered singles are not

statement: The longest zero-volume run shall be counted by row position in stored order (never by calendar days), and among equally long runs the earliest shall be reported, with the UTC dates of its first and last rows.
rationale: consecutive stored rows are exactly what the seam drops together

statement: The post-seam gap shall be measured over the surviving rows (volume > 0 and close not NaN) in stored order: for each consecutive pair more than one calendar day apart, the number of expected sessions strictly between them; the largest such count (earliest on ties) with its two dates, or none when every count is 0.
rationale: zero-volume drops and provider-omitted rows read identically here, which is the point

statement: When the post-seam gap is at least the gap threshold (`--gap-k`, default 5), the status command shall add the NOTE `post-seam continuity: {n} expected session(s) absent between {prev} and {next} - the seam's output splices across this hole; verify the provider era before modelling (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §1)`; it never alerts.
rationale: gap_k=5 is calibrated: the largest true US closure since 1962 measures 4 expected sessions; a hole is a property of the series, not of today's run

statement: The price-resolution measurement shall take the `close_raw` values of rows with volume > 0, drop NaN and non-positive values, keep the newest `--resolution-window` (default 500) of them in stored order (falling back to `close` when that leaves nothing), and when fewer than 60 remain report nothing; otherwise sessions = count, distinct = number of distinct values, min_tick = the smallest (d[k+1] - d[k]) / d[k] over the sorted distinct values (null when only one), flat_share = (consecutive equal pairs) / (sessions - 1).
rationale: measured on close_raw, the provider's own print: the split pass manufactures decimals that were never quoted; below 60 sessions the ratio is noise

statement: When resolution was measured and distinct / sessions < `--resolution-k` (default 0.20) or flat_share > `--flat-k` (default 0.25), the status command shall add the NOTE `coarse price resolution: {distinct} distinct close(s) in {sessions} traded session(s), min tick {tick}, {flat_share:.1%} flat - the provider's quoting grid, verify before modelling (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §7.8)` with tick `{min_tick:.4%}` or `n/a`; it never alerts.
rationale: coarse quoting is a property of an instrument, not a failure of today's run

statement: For each stored row index i from max(1, n - window) to n - 1 (window = `--window`, default 10) whose previous adjusted close is non-zero, the status command shall compute move = close[i] / close[i-1] - 1.0 and, when |move| > `--jump-threshold` (default 0.40, strict) and row i's UTC date is not the date of a stored split (splits are read only for actions-eligible legs), add the ALERT `phantom-split-shaped jump {move:+.1%} on {date} with no same-day split event - check corporate actions (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §2)`.
rationale: the catastrophic input failure for the model is a missed split entering as a crash; this check confirms the preventive machinery worked

statement: For an actions-eligible leg, the status command shall add the ALERT `corporate actions stale: never synced - run jef-data sync` when no splits stamp exists, and the ALERT `corporate actions stale: {n} refresh session(s) missed since {stamp date} - run jef-data sync` when the expected sessions strictly between the stamp's UTC date and today number at least 2 (fixed; not a command option).
rationale: counted in refresh sessions, not wall-clock days, because the refresh rides the weekday leg; both sides are day-quantised so sync and status cannot disagree within a run

statement: A pair report shall hold, in this key order: `asset`, `kind` (`cross_venue`), `a` and `b` (`{exchange}/{symbol}` of the earlier and later leg), `common_session` (YYYY-MM-DD or null), `spread` (float or null), `threshold` (the spread threshold), `alerts`, `warnings`, `notes`.

When a pair cannot be measured, the status command shall add exactly one NOTE and leave common_session and spread null: `{label} has no stored rows - spread not measured` (first empty side, a then b); `no common session in the newest {window} - spread not measured (see the staleness check)`; or `zero mid price on {date} - spread not measured`.
rationale: the per-source check already alerts never-filled; a second alert for the same fact would be noise

statement: The common session of a pair shall be the latest UTC date present in both series' last `--window` stored rows; each side's close is the adjusted `close` of its last stored row on that date; spread = |close_a - close_b| / ((close_a + close_b) / 2), measured whenever the mid is non-zero.
rationale: bounded by the window on purpose: pairing today's close against an ancient one would measure drift

statement: When a spread is measured, the status command shall always add the NOTE `close spread {spread:.4%} on {date} ({a} {close_a:g} vs {b} {close_b:g})`, and when spread > `--spread-threshold` (default 0.005, strict) also the finding `cross-venue close spread {spread:.4%} on {date} exceeds {threshold:.4%} ({a} {close_a:g} vs {b} {close_b:g}) - feed problem or venue distress; verify before acting, never trade it (docs/EVALUATION_CROSS_EXCHANGE.md)` as a WARNING, or as an ALERT when `--spread-alerts` is given.
rationale: a breach compares a cross-check leg; an alert would stop the venue's whole day before it publishes, which a redundancy leg's disagreement does not warrant

statement: The `status --json` document shall be `{"schema_version": 1, "store": store path as text, "reports": [source reports], "pairs": [pair reports], "alerts_total": total alerts over reports and pairs, "warnings_total": total warnings over reports and pairs}` printed with 1-space indentation in that key order; contract status.schema.json.
rationale: a self-describing envelope so the consumer's key lookup finds alerts_total

statement: The status command shall exit 1 when alerts_total > 0 and 0 otherwise; warnings and notes never change the exit code.
rationale: exit 1 stops the venue's day before it publishes

statement: Without `--json`, the status command shall print per source report `{flag} {asset:>6} {exchange}/{symbol}: last {last_session or -}, {missed_sessions or -} missed, {rows or 0} row(s)` with flag `ALERT` (alerts), `WARN ` (warnings, no alert) or `ok   `, then `        res   {distinct} distinct / {sessions} traded, min tick {tick}, {flat_share:.2%} flat` when resolution exists, then `        ALERT {text}`, `        WARN  {text}`, `        note  {text}` lines; per pair `{flag} {asset:>6} cross-venue {a} vs {b}` and its ALERT/WARN/note lines; finally `{n} source(s)` + `, {p} venue pair(s)` (when any) + `, {k} alert(s)` + `, {w} warning(s)` (when any).

The executable `jef-data` shall offer exactly the subcommands validate, sync-actions, load, adjust, import-csv, export, differential, sync, status and universe, with the flags and defaults of contracts/cli.md; a missing subcommand, unknown flag, missing required flag, invalid choice or non-numeric numeric flag shall be an argument error printed by the parser with exit code 2.

A refusal the command wraps (universe, selection, declaration and differential refusals) shall print `{command}: {message}` on stderr and exit 1 with nothing on stdout; any other error escaping a command shall print a Python traceback on stderr and exit 1.
rationale: house pattern, not a traceback

statement: `validate CSV [--min-rows N]` shall read the CSV, print `{csv}: {rows} rows` then the validation report, and exit 0 when the report has no error, else 1.

`universe [--universe PATH]` shall print, per asset, `{name} ({asset_class}, {currency}, threshold {threshold as float})` plus ` [disabled]` for a disabled asset, then per source `  {provider}: {path or symbol}` plus ` [disabled]` for a disabled source plus ` - {note}` when a note exists, and exit 0.

`import-csv --csv F --symbol S [--exchange yahoo] --asset-type {crypto,etf,stock} [--currency USD] [--store data]` shall import per JDL-070 into `exchange/symbol` and print `{csv}: {rows} row(s) -> {store}/market_data/exchange={exchange}/symbol={symbol}/ (price_basis=split_adjusted)` and exit 0; `--asset-type` is required.
rationale: a Yahoo CSV carries no instrument type, so there is no evidence of any kind to infer from

statement: `export --symbol S [--exchange eodhd] --output F [--store data]` shall write the exported frame to F, print `{exchange}/{symbol}: {n} row(s) -> {output}` then the validation report of the exported frame, and exit 0 when that report has no error, else 1; exporting a series with no stored row shall fail with a traceback, exit 1 and no file written.

`adjust --symbol S [--exchange eodhd] [--store data]` shall re-adjust the stored series with the stored splits of S and print `{exchange}/{symbol}: {rows} row(s) re-derived from *_raw with {k} split(s)` and exit 0; a split_adjusted series (AdjustmentRefused) or an empty series (StoreError) shall fail with a traceback and exit 1.

`differential --a-symbol S [--a-exchange eodhd] [--b-symbol S2] [--b-exchange yahoo] [--b-csv F] [--tolerance X] [--output F] [--store data]` (tolerance default of JDL-082) shall compare the exported frame of a/S with the CSV F (preferred when both are given) or with the exported frame of b-exchange/S2, print the report (also written with a trailing newline to --output when given), exit 0 when ok and 1 on findings or unmatched dates, and refuse with `differential: pass --b-csv or --b-symbol` (exit 1) when neither is given.

`load --symbol S [--store data] [--from D] [--to D] [--asset-type T] [--currency USD] [--base-url URL]` shall construct the EODHD collector first (a missing key fails with a traceback, exit 1), normalise S, resolve the declaration per JDL-142, fetch from `--from` or else the day after the latest stored session (whole history when empty) up to `--to`, store the bars in APPEND mode into exchange tag `eodhd` (stored rows win over incoming rows on equal timestamps, only the incoming bars' years are rewritten; raw basis: with the stored splits and EODHD volume raw-ization), re-adjust a raw series that received bars or already had rows, and print `{S as given}: {n incoming bars} bar(s) ingested -> {store}/market_data/`.

If `load` gets no `--asset-type` for a normalised symbol not ending in `.CC`, then it shall refuse with `load: {SYM}: asset_type is required (one of ['crypto', 'etf', 'stock']). The ticker carries no instrument-type signal - SPY, TLT, GLD and IBIT are ETFs spelled exactly like equities - so the old 'stock' default was a guess written into the store as a fact, and TLT is in this repo's universe as an explicit override because that guess got it wrong. Only EODHD's .CC crypto namespace is evidence enough to infer from`; if a `.CC` symbol is declared other than crypto, it shall refuse with `load: {SYM} is in EODHD's .CC crypto namespace but was declared asset_type={T!r}; that combination cannot be true, and guessing either way decides whether split adjustment runs on pre-adjusted prices (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §2)`; a `.CC` symbol with no declaration is crypto; both refusals exit 1 before any fetch or store write.
rationale: the suffix is evidence for crypto in one direction only: crypto does not imply .CC, and a ticker never says stock vs ETF

statement: `sync-actions --symbol S [--store data] [--base-url URL]` (base URL default of JDL-029) shall sync the corporate actions of S per JDL-042 (EODHD key required; a missing key fails with a traceback, exit 1), print `{S}: {s} split(s), {d} dividend(s) -> {store}/corporate_actions/` and exit 0.

`sync [--universe P] [--store P] [--asset A]... [--provider P]... [--dry-run] [--tail N] [--force-actions] [--base-url URL] [--summary-json PATH]` (tail default of JDL-087) shall run the sync with its log lines on stdout, write the summary document (1-space indentation, keys sorted, trailing newline) to PATH after every run that returns - green, red and dry-run alike - and exit 0 when the run is ok, 1 when any leg failed, 1 with `sync: {message}` on stderr (and no summary) on a universe or selection refusal.
rationale: a red run writes the summary too - the always-published breadcrumb

statement: `status [--universe P] [--store P] [--asset A]... [--provider P]... [--staleness N] [--jump-threshold X] [--window N] [--resolution-window N] [--resolution-k X] [--flat-k X] [--gap-k N] [--spread-threshold X] [--spread-alerts] [--json]` (integers N, floats X; defaults are those of JDL-116, JDL-124, JDL-122, JDL-123, JDL-121, JDL-129) shall print the JSON envelope or the table and exit per JDL-131; a universe or selection refusal shall print `status: {message}` on stderr and exit 1.

The chain `daily.sh` shall run under `set -euo pipefail` and read JEF_S3_BUCKET (required), JEF_ASSETS (default `AAPL BTC TLT NVDA TSLA IBM`, split on whitespace), JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST, ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4, JEF_TASK_VCPU, JEF_TASK_MEMORY_GB, JEF_RUN_STAMP and JEF_APP_DIR (default `/app`); EODHD_API_KEY passes through to the commands it runs; RUN_DATE = `date -u +%F`, STORE = `data`, OUT = `out/{RUN_DATE}`, DIAG = `{OUT}/.diagnostics`.

When JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST is empty or unset, the chain shall fetch `curl -s "${ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4:-}/task"` once (failure tolerated) and set JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST to Containers[0].ImageDigest, else Containers[0].ImageID, else `unknown` (also when parsing fails), and set JEF_TASK_VCPU to Limits.CPU and JEF_TASK_MEMORY_GB to Limits.Memory / 1024 (Python float text) only when unset and parsing succeeds, exporting both; JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST is exported in every case, before the exec guard.
rationale: one metadata fetch for both facts; set-if-unset so the re-exec never recomputes and an external value passes through

statement: The chain shall set JEF_RUN_STAMP to `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ` only when it is unset or empty and export it before the exec guard, so every stage of one invocation (and the re-exec) shares one stamp.
rationale: the chain's start instant, captured once

statement: When the chain is invoked with arguments whose first is not `--inner`, it shall `exec` those arguments as a command (inheriting the digest and stamp exports) and run none of its own stages, traps or uploads; the command's exit code becomes the chain's.
rationale: ECS cannot replace an ENTRYPOINT at run-task, so an override command arrives as arguments and must exec through instead of being swallowed

statement: When invoked without arguments, the chain shall re-exec itself as `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=60 3600 "$0" --inner`; all stages run only in the `--inner` invocation.
rationale: a wedged run must die loudly, not hold the lock all day

statement: If JEF_S3_BUCKET is empty or unset in the inner run, then the chain shall stop with the shell parameter error whose text ends `JEF_S3_BUCKET must name the venue bucket` and exit code 1, before sourcing the externals, installing traps or running any stage.

The chain shall source `events.sh` and `dashboard.sh` from its own directory (`dirname "$0"`) before changing directory, then `cd` to JEF_APP_DIR, print `== jef daily {RUN_DATE} assets: {assets space-separated}` and create `{DIAG}` (`mkdir -p`); it uses only the externals' functions `jef_emit STAGE RC T0 T1 [args...]`, `jef_put STAGE`, `jef_attach_if_present PATH`, `jef_manifest_keys MANIFEST OUT` and `jef_publish_dashboard`, which read RUN_DATE, STORE, JEF_RUN_STAMP, JEF_S3_BUCKET, JEF_EVENT_DIR and JEF_DASH_DIR; the externals are given, not specified here.
rationale: $0 is relative to the invoking directory, so dirname $0 stops resolving once the script changes directory

statement: After sourcing, the chain shall install a TERM trap running `jef_emit "${STAGE:-unknown}" 143 "${STAGE_T0:-0}" "$(date +%s)"`, `jef_put "${STAGE:-unknown}"`, `exit 143`, and an EXIT trap running `jef_publish_dashboard` (which returns 0, so the run's exit code is preserved) - the dashboard therefore publishes on green and red exits of the inner run alike, never for an exec'd override.
rationale: emit what the dying stage knows inside the 60 s grace; the dashboard publishes on every exit so the page shows a red day within minutes

statement: The chain shall first restore the store with `aws s3 sync s3://{bucket}/store/ data/ --only-show-errors` (a failure stops the chain with its exit code) and build the filter arguments `--asset A` for each asset in order.

The sync stage shall set STAGE=sync and STAGE_T0=`date +%s`, run `jef-data sync {filters} --store data --summary-json out/{RUN_DATE}/.diagnostics/sync.json` capturing its exit code, call `jef_emit sync {rc} {t0} {date +%s}` with `--attach {that file}` appended only when the file is non-empty, call `jef_put sync`, and exit with rc when rc is non-zero.

The status stage shall set STAGE=status, run `jef-data status {filters} --store data --json` once with its stdout both printed and written to `out/{RUN_DATE}/.diagnostics/status.json` (the pipeline's exit code is the status command's), emit and put the `status` stage like the sync stage, and exit with rc when non-zero.
rationale: one evaluation, captured: running status twice would evaluate the freshness predicate at two instants

statement: The binning stage shall set STAGE=binning and, per asset in order, run `jef-binning --asset A --store data --counter-start latest --counter-end latest --output-dir out/{RUN_DATE}/A`, find the first `run_manifest*.json` directly inside that directory, when found call `jef_manifest_keys {manifest} out/{RUN_DATE}/.diagnostics/binning-A.json`, call `jef_emit binning {a_rc} {a_t0} {t1} --asset A` plus `--manifest {m} --manifest-root out/{RUN_DATE} --manifest-prefix runs/{RUN_DATE}` when a manifest was found plus `--attach` of the keys file when non-empty, and stop the loop at the first non-zero rc; then call `jef_put binning` once and exit with that rc when non-zero.
rationale: one ledger object for the stage, one emit per asset; a failing asset still emits

statement: Only when every stage exited 0, the chain shall run `aws s3 sync data/ s3://{bucket}/store/ --only-show-errors`, `aws s3 sync out/{RUN_DATE}/ s3://{bucket}/runs/{RUN_DATE}/ --only-show-errors`, pipe `{JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST}` plus newline into `aws s3 cp - s3://{bucket}/runs/{RUN_DATE}/image_digest.txt --only-show-errors`, print `== green ({JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST})` and exit 0; a red stage publishes neither the store nor the run outputs.
rationale: publish ONLY on green: a red run publishes nothing and the task exit code feeds the alarm
